reuse.why: Moves the skipWeekend gate into getDateWithSkippedWeekend, adds shared skipsWeekendOccurrences/isNonWorkingDay/getDailyTakeCount and a day-string wrapper that schedule-template now uses instead of its own ternaries.

duplication.why: The predicates are shared, but the 'daily: filter off-days, else move' dispatch (dropsWeekendDays ? filter(!isNonWorkingDay) : getDateWithSkippedWeekend) is still written out separately in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange.

placement.why: All rule pieces live in shared/schedules.ts; only the skip-vs-move dispatch remains in the server handlers, and frequency/holidays are added to rschedule data in rule-utils so the shared code can see them.

scope.why: Focused on schedule date handling across the five steps with thorough tests; no unrelated edits.

maintainability.why: Named helpers and constants make the rule mostly single-sourced, though the dispatch repeated at three sites and the double skipWeekend check in getDayWithSkippedWeekend leave some drift risk.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange each decide skip-vs-move around getDateWithSkippedWeekend rather than calling one function for the final occurrence decision; schedule-template routes through the noSkipWeekend flag.

disguised_duplication.where: The daily drop/move dispatch is reshaped per site: `.find` + early return in getNextDate, ternary filter/slice vs map in getUpcomingDates, `continue` + nested ternary in getDatesInRange.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains skipWeekend and holidays parameters; the daily-skip special case is handled outside it at getNextDate (shared/schedules.ts), getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange (server/schedules/app.ts).
